statement: Determine whether six distinct nonzero rational numbers can form a D(1) tuple with at least two integer elements.
assumptions: Squares are rational squares, including zero.
The six elements themselves are distinct and nonzero.
Treat the positive subcase and arbitrary-sign case separately.
quantifiers: For every 1<=i<j<=6, ai*aj+1 belongs to Q^2.
At least two distinct elements belong to Z.
objective: Find a completely verified witness or prove nonexistence in the declared full domain; retain rigorous partial results otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Existence requires explicit reduced fractions and all fifteen exact roots.
Nonexistence requires an unbounded argument, not a finite parameter search.
Reject zero elements and repeated elements even when all pairwise tests pass.
scope_exclusion: This is over Q, not the ring of integers of Q(zeta_7).
